contexts.name: Agile & Scrum
contexts.description: Kanban boards, To Do / In Progress / Done, blockers, Daily Standups and Sprint planning.

contexts.name: Mentorship
contexts.description: The two-way mentor/mentee relationship: guidance, learning from mistakes and professional growth.

contexts.name: Workplace Communication
contexts.description: Handling conflicts respectfully, giving feedback without criticism and fostering collaboration.

items.definition: To give someone authority or confidence.
items.example: Good Scrum Masters empower the team to make their own decisions.

items.definition: To encourage the development of something.
items.example: Daily standups help foster trust within the team.

items.definition: To show the way.
items.example: She guided the new developer during his first sprint.

items.definition: To make an action or process easier.
items.example: The Scrum Master facilitates the sprint planning meeting.

items.definition: To agree or coordinate with others.
items.example: We need to align with the QA team before the release.

items.definition: To communicate a message or feeling.
items.example: It was hard to convey the urgency of the bug to the client.

items.definition: To think about and begin to deal with an issue.
items.example: We should address this blocker before the end of the day.

items.definition: To give support or confidence to someone.
items.example: I always encourage my mentees to ask questions.

items.definition: To accept or admit the existence or truth of something.
items.example: The lead acknowledged that the estimate was too optimistic.

items.definition: To make a statement less confusing.
items.example: Could you clarify the acceptance criteria for this story?

items.definition: To grow or develop well.
items.example: Junior developers thrive when they get constructive feedback.

items.definition: To improve the quality or value of something.
items.example: Adding E2E tests enhanced the stability of the app.

items.definition: To try to acquire or develop a quality or skill.
items.example: He is cultivating his leadership skills by mentoring others.

items.definition: To succeed in dealing with a problem.
items.example: The team overcame the deployment issues in two days.

items.definition: To propel or carry along.
items.example: Clear goals drive positive growth in the team.

items.definition: To take responsibility for something and take action.
items.example: When the lead got sick, Ana stepped up and ran the daily.

items.definition: To resolve a problem or difficulty.
items.example: Let's sort out the merge conflicts before the demo.

items.definition: To help someone understand or do something difficult.
items.example: I guided him through the deployment process step by step.

items.definition: To discover information.
items.example: We need to find out why the tests are failing.

items.definition: To reconcile after an argument.
items.example: After the heated retro, they made up over coffee.

items.definition: To accept (a challenge or responsibility).
items.example: She decided to take on the migration to the new API.

items.definition: To have the same understanding or knowledge.
items.example: Let's have a quick call to make sure we're on the same page.

items.definition: To act first or take charge of a situation.
items.example: I'll take the lead on the frontend refactor.

items.definition: Fully concentrating on what is being said.
items.example: Active listening is key during one-on-ones with your mentee.

items.definition: Useful comments and suggestions that contribute to a positive outcome.
items.example: The code review gave me constructive feedback on my tests.

items.definition: Choices made based on good information and understanding.
items.example: Metrics from the last sprint help us make informed decisions.

items.definition: 100% certainty that something IS happening now.
items.example: She is not replying, she must be busy.

items.definition: 100% certainty that something is IMPOSSIBLE now.
items.example: They are laughing, they can't be arguing.

items.definition: 100% certainty that something happened.
items.example: The code works, they must have fixed the bug.

items.definition: 100% certainty that something did NOT happen.
items.example: He didn't know about the meeting; he can't have read the email.

items.term: might have / could have + past participle
items.definition: Possibility or uncertainty about the past.
items.example: They might have reached an agreement, but I'm not sure.

items.definition: Expresses purpose. Use 'could' for past actions and 'can' for present.
items.example: I used a Kanban board so that we could stay organized.

items.definition: Expresses purpose.
items.example: In order to achieve success, we must build trust.

items.definition: Introduces a contrast inside the same sentence.
items.example: Although building this bond takes time, it is worth it.

items.definition: Introduces a contrast with the previous sentence; used with a comma.
items.example: The project was difficult. However, we finished on time.

items.definition: Introduces a consequence.
items.example: Mentors share experiences; as a result, the team grows.

items.definition: Introduces a logical consequence.
items.example: The server crashed. Therefore, we lost the data.
